page: PDF 278 / printed 258 (figure note) vs PDF 274 / printed 254 (prose)
issue: The figure's note states 'Feasible max = 40 rps × 624,000 active s/mo = 24.96M req/mo' (40 × 624,000 = 24,960,000 — correct), but the prose on printed p. 254 states 'the canonical active window of 62,000 active seconds/month (6.24M requests = 10 rps × 8 h), so the most it can serve is 40 rps × 62,000 s = 2,480,000 active s/month = 24.96M requests/month'. 40 × 62,000 = 2,480,000 REQUESTS, not 'active s/month'; 2,480,000 × 10 rps = 24.8M, not 24.96M; and 10 rps × 8 h = 288,000 s = 2.88M requests, not 6.24M. The figure's note is the arithmetically correct form, so the prose must be corrected to match it — but as printed, the figure and the prose that explains it disagree on the single number that sets the plot's right edge.
evidence: Figure note (PDF 278): 'Feasible max = 40 rps × 624,000 active s/mo = 24.96M req/mo'. Printed p. 254: '62,000 active seconds/month (6.24M requests = 10 rps × 8 h)' and '40 rps × 62,000 s = 2,480,000 active s/month = 24.96M requests/month'.
acceptance_test: Correct printed p. 254 to '624,000 active seconds/month' and '40 rps × 624,000 s = 24.96M requests/month', and either drop '(6.24M requests = 10 rps × 8 h)' or replace it with the correct decomposition (6.24M / 10 rps = 624,000 s = 173.3 h). Confirm the figure note and the prose then agree exactly.

issue: The x-axis is 'Requests/month (log) — duration varied at FIXED 40 rps peak', but the two anchors on that axis use different rates: the canonical point 6.24M req/mo is 10 rps over the active window (printed p. 254), while the feasible max 24.96M req/mo is 40 rps over the same window (figure note). So 'requests/month' is not a single-valued function of the varied quantity (duration), and a reader cannot tell which rate maps a given x-position to a duration. The natural reading (x = 40 rps × duration) puts the canonical point at 156,000 s, contradicting the 624,000 s window.
evidence: X-axis label 'Requests/month (log) — duration varied at FIXED 40 rps peak, FIXED 21-host fleet'; note 'Feasible max = 40 rps × 624,000 active s/mo = 24.96M req/mo'; printed p. 254 '6.24M requests = 10 rps × 8 h'.
acceptance_test: State the rate basis on the axis or in the note (e.g. 'x = requests/month at 10 rps average; peak 40 rps; feasible max = 40 rps × 624,000 s'), and confirm the canonical point and the feasible max are derived from one stated rate basis.

issue: The price band is encoded as a red/pink diagonal band and the infeasible region as a grey diagonal hatch; in grayscale both become mid-grey diagonal textures, so the band can be mistaken for the infeasible region or for the band edges. The band also relies on hue for its identity in the legend (pink filled swatch) while the plotted band appears striped.
evidence: Rendered page: red diagonal band across the plot; grey diagonal hatch right of the 24.96M dotted line; legend swatch is a solid pink rectangle.
acceptance_test: Convert to grayscale and confirm the band and the infeasible region are distinguishable at 100% zoom; if not, give the infeasible region a distinct fill (solid light grey or cross-hatch) and/or outline the band.

issue: The eight-line assumption note under the plot is set noticeably smaller than the caption and appears to fall below the 8 pt floor for figure annotations; at 150 dpi the smallest lines ('Not re-sized per volume: a frozen-fleet cost, not a scalable crossover.') are only marginally legible.
evidence: Note block under FIGURE 16.1, 8 lines, visibly smaller than the caption text.
acceptance_test: Confirm the note's computed font size is ≥ 8.0 pt in the source; if not, raise it or move the note into the caption/body text.

issue: Prose states the figure marks the break-even mid-point with a star and the sensitivity span with a horizontal line; neither mark is resolvable in the 150 dpi render, and a span line drawn at y = $155,816.93 would be exactly coincident with the blue self-host line and therefore invisible as a separate mark.
evidence: Printed 257 (PDF 277), quoted: 'The figure marks the mid-point (star) and the full sensitivity span (horizontal line), annotates the feasible bound (24.96M = 40 rps x 624,000 active s), and shades the infeasible region beyond it.' In the render the feasible-bound annotation ('feasible max 24.96M' + arrow), the shaded infeasible region and the 'INFEASIBLE (> 24.96M)' label are all clearly present; a star at (7.49M, 1.558e5) and a 6.23M-10.39M span indicator distinct from the blue line are not. NOT VERIFIED against the vector source. Semantic arithmetic that IS verified: 155,816.93 / 0.0208 = 7,491,198 ~= 7.5M; / 0.025 = 6,232,677 ~= 6.2M; / 0.015 = 10,387,795 ~= 10.4M; 40 x 624,000 = 24,960,000 = 24.96M - all match the figure's annotations.
root_cause: Either the markers are drawn too small/low-contrast to survive a 150 dpi raster, or the span line is drawn coincident with the self-host cost line, or the prose describes marks that were removed.
correction: Open the figure source. If a star and a span indicator exist, make the span visually separable from the blue self-host line (e.g. a bracket with end ticks offset below the line) so it reads as a distinct mark. If they do not exist, delete the '(star)' and '(horizontal line)' clauses from printed 257.
acceptance_test: Vector source contains a star marker at the 7.49M break-even and a span indicator covering 6.23M-10.39M that is distinguishable from the blue self-host line at print size; OR the printed 257 sentence no longer claims those two marks.

issue: The full-page Figure 16.1 float splits the §16.8 end-of-chapter mini-case mid-sentence across a figure page.
evidence: Printed 257 (PDF 277) ends mid-clause: '...a startup's 0.5-FTE operator (~$26K/mo - ~= $62K/yr fully loaded for one engineer, a scenario value'. Printed 258 (PDF 278) is entirely the Figure 16.1 plot + assumptions block + caption, with blank space below the caption and no body text. The sentence resumes on printed 259. The reader must turn two pages to finish one sentence, in the chapter's closing section.

correction: Move the float so it does not interrupt §16.8: place it at the top of printed 257 (before §16.7/§16.8 begin) or defer it to immediately after the mini-case concludes. Do not leave it as a page-interior break inside a sentence.
acceptance_test: No sentence or paragraph in §16.7–§16.8 is split by the Figure 16.1 float; printed 257 ends at a paragraph or section boundary, and the figure's caption remains adjacent to the figure.

figure: Figure 17.1 — Sizing a fleet of one model
issue: The figure is over-annotated: two long top annotations repeat the same ρ = 0.85 residual calculation, the title and subtitle both repeat the ideal ρ = 1 / no-SLO caveat, and the small text reduces legibility at print size.
evidence: The top annotation 'N = 4 fleet (~8.0, ideal) at ρ = 0.85 the residual = ~5.1 < ~5.5, need ≥ 0.917.' and the second annotation 'N-1 clears the burst only at ρ = 1: at ρ = 0.85 it is 3 × 2.0 × 0.85 ≈ 5.1 req/s, below the ~5.5 burst (ρ ≥ 0.917 is needed to clear it)' state the same calculation. The title says 'ideal ρ = 1 analytical ceilings' and the subtitle says 'Ideal ρ = 1 analytical ceiling — no SLO claim.'; the caption repeats the same scope. The rendered 150 dpi page shows these annotations at roughly 13–14 px line height (~6.2–6.7 pt).
acceptance_test: Keep one top annotation (or move the calculation to the caption), remove the duplicate title/subtitle caveat, and ensure every remaining in-figure label is at least 8 pt at 100% print size with no crowding.

figure: FIGURE 17.1 — Sizing a fleet of one model
issue: The caption's failover caveat contains a self-contradictory arithmetic statement: 'the N = 1 residual (~6 req/s) clears the burst only at ρ = 1 — at ρ = 0.85 it is 3 × 2.0 = 6.0 rps, below the ~5.5 burst (ρ = 0.917 is needed to clear it)'. 6.0 rps is ABOVE the 5.5 burst, not below it; the ρ = 0.85 value is 0.85 × 6.0 = 5.1 rps. As printed, the sentence asserts the residual fails at ρ = 1 while the figure draws it at 6.0 rps above the 5.5 burst — a reader can conclude the failover case is infeasible even at ideal utilization, which is the opposite of the drawn geometry.
evidence: Caption (PDF 283): 'at ρ = 0.85 it is 3 × 2.0 = 6.0 rps, below the ~5.5 burst (ρ = 0.917 is needed to clear it)'; figure draws the residual line at y = 6 and the burst peak at 5.5; 5.5 / 6.0 = 0.9167.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as 'at ρ = 0.85 the residual delivers 0.85 × 6.0 = 5.1 rps, below the ~5.5 burst; ρ ≥ 0.917 is needed to clear it'. Confirm the corrected sentence is consistent with the drawn 6.0 and 5.5 levels.

issue: The legend and caption label the residual line 'N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' and 'the N = 1 residual (~6 req/s)'. 'N = 1' reads as 'one host serving', which contradicts the drawn value 6.0 rps (three hosts × 2.0) and the parenthetical '1 host drains'. The book's own failover vocabulary elsewhere is 'N−1 single-host failover' (printed p. 256), so the figure introduces a second, contradictory notation for the same event.
evidence: Legend entry 'N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' at y = 6; caption 'the N = 1 residual (~6 req/s)'; printed p. 256 'failover = N−1 single-host failover is modeled'.
acceptance_test: Relabel the legend entry and the caption as 'N−1 residual (one host drains, ideal)' and confirm no occurrence of 'N = 1 residual' remains in Ch 17.

issue: The grey shaded band across the top of the plot (roughly y = 8 to 12) carries the label 'ideal ρ = 1 analytical ceiling — no SLO claim', which describes a LINE, not a band. The band is neither in the legend nor mentioned in the caption. A reader will most likely read it as the overload region (offered load above the N = 4 capacity of 8.0), in which case the label is wrong; or as a 'ceiling band', in which case the blue 8.0 line is the ceiling and the label is misplaced. Either reading is a misreading of the figure's intent, and the caption's 'every capacity line is an ideal ρ = 1 analytical service ceiling' does not describe it.
evidence: Plot shows a light grey/blue filled region above the blue 'N = 4 fleet capacity (~8.0, ideal)' line, with the text 'ideal ρ = 1 analytical ceiling — no SLO claim' inside it at the upper right; the caption mentions only the burst, the one-host bound, the N = 4 line and the N = 1 residual.
acceptance_test: Either relabel the band 'overload: offered load > N = 4 capacity (8.0 req/s)' and add it to the caption, or remove it and move the 'no SLO claim' caveat to a leader on the capacity lines. Confirm the caption describes every drawn element.

issue: The caption claims 'the same rule sizes the canonical 40 rps peak to 21 hosts (Ch. 17-20)', but the figure's own arithmetic does not exhibit that rule: ceil(5.5 / 2.0) = 3 hosts, yet the figure sizes 4 hosts (8.0 req/s); and ceil(40 / 2.0) = 20, yet the canonical fleet is 21. The rule that actually produces both numbers (ceil(peak / per-host ceiling) + 1 reserve) is never stated, and the figure shows no working-host count, so the reader cannot see why 4 rather than 3 — the exact question the figure exists to answer.
evidence: Caption: 'the same rule sizes the canonical 40 rps peak to 21 hosts (Ch. 17-20)'; figure: one-host bound 2.0, N = 4 capacity 8.0, burst 5.5; printed p. 256 'the 32-host = 31 working + 1 reserve policy line'.
acceptance_test: State the sizing rule explicitly in the caption (e.g. 'N = ceil(peak / 2.0) + 1 reserve: 3 + 1 = 4 here, 20 + 1 = 21 for the canonical 40 rps peak') and add the working-host count to the figure's N = 4 label.

issue: The y-axis is labelled 'offered load (req/s)' although three of the four drawn series are capacity ceilings, not offered load; and the x-axis 'time of day' carries no unit (hours? a normalized index?) while the bell-shaped burst curve has no stated functional form, so its shape can be read as a modelled load profile rather than a schematic.
evidence: Y-axis 'offered load (req/s)'; x-axis 'time of day' with ticks 0–10; bell-shaped red curve with no formula in caption or note.
acceptance_test: Relabel the y-axis 'load / capacity (req/s)' and the x-axis 'time of day (h, schematic)', and state in the caption that the burst shape is illustrative.

issue: Two drawn elements are not keyed: the green 'headroom' label and the red 'failover' label (the latter with no leader, so it is unclear whether it annotates the 2.0–6.0 gap or the residual line). In grayscale the orange dashed residual line and the grey dashed one-host bound differ mainly in lightness, and the red 'failover' text shares its color with the red 'one host cannot meet the burst on its own' text.
evidence: Legend has four entries (offered load, N = 4 capacity, one host bound, N = 1 residual); 'headroom' in green and 'failover' in red appear only in-plot.
acceptance_test: Add the two annotations to the legend or give them leaders, and differentiate the two dashed lines by dash pattern (long-dash vs short-dash) rather than hue alone; verify in grayscale.

issue: Near the burst peak the orange label 'burst peak = 5.5 req/s' and the green 'headroom' label sit within roughly one line-height of each other at x ≈ 6.5–9, and 'headroom' is not attached to any marked quantity (the headroom is 8.0 − 5.5 = 2.5 req/s), so the reader cannot tell what quantity the word names.
evidence: Rendered page: 'burst peak = 5.5 req/s' at y ≈ 5.5 and 'headroom' at y ≈ 5.9 immediately above/right of it.
acceptance_test: Move 'headroom' into the gap between the 5.5 peak and the 8.0 line and label it with the value ('headroom 2.5 req/s'); confirm no label collisions at 300 dpi.

issue: The caption links the figure's 4-host fleet to 'the same rule' that yields '~21 hosts' for the canonical peak, but the two numbers are on different bases: the rule alone gives 3 hosts for the 5.5 req/s burst, and the drawn N = 4 includes the +1 N-1 failover reserve, which applied to the canonical peak would give 22 (the book's case (ii)), not 21.
evidence: Caption, quoted: 'a small ~5.5 req/s burst exceeds one host's ~2.0 req/s analytical bound, so a 4-host fleet (~8.0 req/s) is sized above it ... the same rule sizes the canonical 40 rps peak to ~21 hosts'. Re-derivation: 3 x 2.0 = 6.0 >= 5.5, so 3 hosts already clear the burst at rho = 1 without the fourth; the figure's own annotations ('N-1 clears the burst only at rho = 1', 'headroom', 'failover') show the fourth host is the N-1 reserve. Table 17-1 (PDF 290 / printed 270) gives N_min = ceil(lambda_peak . W / (C . u . rho)) = ceil(40 x 8.6 / 17) = 20.24 -> 21 with N_spare added separately; printed 253-254 price a 22-host case (ii) = 21 + 1 reserve. So 'the same rule' produces 3 (burst) and 21 (canonical), while the figure shows 4 and the caption implies the figure's 4 follows from that rule.
root_cause: Caption conflates the base sizing rule (N_min) with the failover-inclusive count actually drawn (N_min + N_spare).
correction: State the two steps explicitly, e.g.: '3 hosts clear the 5.5 req/s burst at rho = 1; a 4th is the N-1 reserve so that 3 still clear it after one host drains - the same +1 reserve that turns the canonical 21 into the 22-host case (ii).' Alternatively drop the 'same rule -> ~21 hosts' juxtaposition from this caption.
acceptance_test: A reader can reproduce both host counts from the caption alone and can say which of the two (3 or 4; 21 or 22) each sentence refers to, with N_min and N_min + N_spare never used interchangeably.

issue: Legend entries 1 and 2 use identical solid line samples distinguished only by hue (red vs blue); in grayscale both render as solid dark lines, so the legend samples alone cannot be matched to their series.
evidence: Legend row 1, quoted: 'offered load (burst)' (red solid sample) and 'N = 4 fleet capacity (~8.0, ideal)' (blue solid sample). Entries 2 and 4 ('one host bound (~2.0, ideal)' dash-dot, 'N-1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' dotted) are style-distinguishable. In the plot the two solid series remain separable by shape (time-varying curve vs horizontal ceiling at y = 8), so the figure is recoverable, but the legend relies on color alone for a same-style pair.
root_cause: Line style was not varied for the two solid series.
correction: Give one of the two solid series a distinct treatment that survives grayscale - e.g. render the N = 4 capacity line as a long-dash solid, or add a marker to the offered-load curve - so each legend sample is unique without hue.
acceptance_test: Convert the page to grayscale: every one of the four legend samples is distinguishable from every other by line style or marker alone, without relying on hue.

issue: The in-plot annotation identifies the ~6.0 req/s N-1 residual line as 'dash-dot', but the legend renders that series as dotted and reserves dash-dot for the one-host bound at ~2.0 req/s.
evidence: Annotation at top of plot, quoted: 'N-1 clears the burst only at rho = 1 (dash-dot line at the rho = 1 ideal, ~6.0): at rho = 0.85 the residual = ~5.1 < ~5.5, need >= 0.917.' Legend, quoted: '... N-1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' with a dotted sample, versus 'one host bound (~2.0, ideal)' with a dash-dot sample. In the render the horizontal line at y ~= 6 is dotted and the line at y ~= 2 is dash-dot; there is no dash-dot line at ~6.0.
root_cause: Line-style descriptor in the annotation was not kept in sync with the legend/plot series styles.
correction: Change 'dash-dot' to 'dotted' in the annotation (matching the legend and render), or change the legend sample and rendered style of the N-1 residual series to dash-dot and leave the one-host bound as the only dotted/differently-styled series. Whichever is chosen, annotation, legend sample and rendered line must agree.
acceptance_test: For the ~6.0 N-1 residual series, the annotation's style word, the legend's sample glyph and the rendered line style are identical; dash-dot appears in the figure for exactly one series.

issue: Row C's derivation uses 24.9037 GB per whole context without stating the context length it represents, so the number cannot be independently checked from the table; the implied length must be confirmed against the canonical whole-context used elsewhere because C = 17 (not 18) is what produces the canonical 21 hosts.
evidence: Table 17-1 row C, quoted: 'per-host whole-context KV slots: 436 GB / 24.9037 GB = 17.51 -> floor 17' | '17 slots'. Arithmetic checks: 436 / 24.9037 = 17.5074 -> 17.51 -> floor 17 (correct), and 40 x 8.6 / 17 = 20.24 -> 21 hosts (correct). But 24,903.7 MB / 2.62144 MB per token (the book's canonical FP16 full-MHA 70B KV per token) = 9,500.0 tokens exactly, i.e. the table silently assumes a 9,500-token whole context. The book elsewhere derives 1,200 + 8,000 = 9,200 as an in-book token sum; if 9,200 were the KV whole-context, per-context KV = 24.117 GB, C = floor(436 / 24.117) = 18, and the canonical host count becomes ceil(40 x 8.6 / 18) = 20, not 21. The exact 9,500 match makes the benign reading (8,000 in + 1,500 out = 9,500) likely, but the table never says so. NOT VERIFIED against Chs. 4/17/20 in this pass.
root_cause: The derivation shows the division but omits the quantity being divided into (context tokens), so the one input a reader needs in order to re-derive C is missing.
correction: Add the context length to the Meaning cell, e.g. '436 GB / 24.9037 GB (9,500-token whole context at 2.62 MB/token FP16 full-MHA) = 17.51 -> floor 17', and confirm that 9,500 is the same whole-context used in the Ch. 4 workload table and the Ch. 17/20 host counts.
acceptance_test: Table 17-1 states the token count behind 24.9037 GB; that token count matches the canonical whole-context stated in Ch. 4 / Table 4-2; and re-deriving C and N_min from the stated context reproduces 17 slots and 21 hosts.
